items.s: Looking at maps before a trip gives many people real ____, and they smile as they plan.
A small restaurant cannot stay open without enough ____ who pay for their meals.
The biggest ____ of travelling with small children is keeping them busy on long journeys.
Some people think tourists are the ____ of a quiet village, but others say they bring money.
We left the viewpoint early because the ____ of people made it impossible to see anything.

items.s: Last summer we ____ to a small beach that we saw in a video.
A friend ____ me a video of a town in Italy yesterday.
He ____ a lovely view and stopped to take a photo.
Before the video, we ____ anything about that beach.

tfn.s: In the video, the sand on the beach looks almost empty.
tfn.why: The text says: "the sand is almost empty".

tfn.s: When the traveller arrives at the beach, nobody else is there.
tfn.why: The text says there is "a line of about twenty people" waiting.

tfn.s: The traveller takes a photo on the beach.
tfn.why: The text does not say whether the traveller takes a photo.

tfn.s: In the survey, nearly four in ten travellers had visited a place mainly to take a photo or video.
tfn.why: The text says: "nearly four in ten had visited a place mainly in order to take a photo or a video".

tfn.s: The writer says photographs are bad for every holiday.
tfn.why: The text says: "None of this makes photographs the enemy".

focus.note: Some words always go with one small word. Learn them as a pair: afraid of, depend on, interested in.

items.s: Many travellers are afraid ____ missing the best view.
Choosing a hotel often depends ____ the price and the view.
I'm terrible ____ taking photos in the dark.
She is interested ____ villages that tourists don't know.
The village is famous ____ its beautiful old bridge.
Several ____ complained that the new viewpoint had made their quiet street impossible to walk along.
Cropping a photo to hide a crowd is not necessarily ____; most photographers simply choose the best part of the scene.
Photos are often shown to friends as ____ that a trip really happened.
The ____ of social media on where people choose to travel is hard to measure exactly.
Taking twenty photos of the same plate is quite normal ____ these days, and nobody finds it strange.
Booking the flight made the ____ of seeing the island feel real for the first time.

match.d: chosen to reflect the whole country
too many people in one place

items.s: By the time we reached the viewpoint, the sun ____ already.
The street ____ so often that everyone recognises it.
If we ____ about the crowds, we would have chosen another beach.
You ____ to hurry; the viewpoint stays open until midnight.
If the crowds keep growing, the town ____ a limit on visitors.

tfn.s: Fewer than half of the travellers surveyed said they had visited a tourist site mainly to take a photo or video.
tfn.why: The text gives the figure as 39%, which is under half.

tfn.s: The writer says taking photographs of a holiday stops people enjoying it.
tfn.why: The text says: "Nor is photographing a holiday the opposite of enjoying it".

tfn.s: Most of the travellers in the survey were under thirty.
tfn.why: The text does not give the ages of the travellers.

tfn.s: The text says a café can end up serving visitors from countries its owner has never been to.
tfn.why: The text says a popular video can bring "visitors from countries its owner has never been to".

tfn.s: The text says all residents agree that a busy summer is a problem.
tfn.why: The text says: "Residents are not one group with one opinion".

focus.note: Many verbs need a fixed preposition after them: object to, benefit from, rely on. Learn the verb and the preposition together.

items.s: Many locals object ____ crowds blocking their streets.
Small businesses often benefit ____ a sudden rise in visitors.
Residents protested ____ the closure of their local bakery to make room for a souvenir shop.
Travel writers are sometimes blamed ____ spoiling quiet villages.
Many visitors rely ____ their phones to find the way.
Editing out the crowd is hardly ____ when every viewer knows that a photograph shows only part of a scene.
The group's ____ was so packed with famous viewpoints that nobody had a free afternoon.
Without the festival, many family restaurants would have struggled to attract enough ____ in winter.
There was a noticeable ____ between those who wanted to linger and those who wanted to keep moving.
The ____ for an undiscovered village often ends with a crowd arriving in the same lanes.
Short videos have an astonishing ____, travelling far beyond the audience of the person who posted them.

match.d: someone or something that settles a decision
something that makes an effect stronger
useful because it teaches you something
the problem of too many people in a place

items.s: Her ____ on waiting for perfect light tested the whole group's patience.
The idea that a place can stay secret for ever is simply ____ once a video has been posted.
Local shopkeepers have mixed feelings about the sudden ____ of their street.
Viewers tend to ____ how peaceful a place will be when they have only seen it in a photograph.
It is ____ to arrive early if you want a clear view of the footbridge.

tfn.s: The writer is cautious about how much the 39% survey result proves.
tfn.why: The text calls it "one industry survey reporting what people say about themselves, not proof".

tfn.s: The writer thinks the disagreement over the sunset is best settled by deciding which traveller is right.
The writer believes social media will eventually reduce the number of people who travel.
tfn.why: The text makes no prediction about how many people will travel.

tfn.s: The text suggests that a popular post can be good news for one person and bad news for another on the same street.
tfn.why: The post can bring "badly needed custom" to a restaurant yet leave a neighbour "trying to park".

tfn.s: The writer recommends searching for an undiscovered place as a way of avoiding crowds.
tfn.why: The text says that hunt "is what empties the quiet places".

focus.note: At C1, adjectives often take a fixed preposition that is hard to guess: tantamount to, fraught with, contingent on. Treat each pair as one unit.

items.s: Choosing a destination only because it is popular online is tantamount ____ letting a stranger plan your holiday.
The journey proved fraught ____ small frustrations, from cancelled trains to a closed viewpoint.
Whether a village copes with sudden fame is contingent ____ how far its residents are consulted.
A harbour bereft ____ its fishing boats may look tidy in photographs but loses part of its character.
The long climb culminated ____ a breathtaking view of the harbour.

speak.title: Role-play: one famous beach or a quiet day
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You saw a video of a beautiful beach and you saved it. You want to spend the whole day there and take photos. Explain why it matters to you, and listen to your friend's worries.

b.role: the friend who wants a quiet day
b.text: You've heard the beach will be packed. You'd prefer a slow lunch somewhere nobody told you about. Say what worries you, then suggest a plan you can both accept.

phrases: I'd love to see that beach from the video.
It's going to be packed, though.
We don't have to take a hundred photos.
How about half a day there and half somewhere quiet?
That's fair, I'm happy to compromise.
What matters most to you on this trip?
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: where did you decide to go, and how did you share the time?
